graphEvents.label: What does the packet already enforce?
Fail-closed pre-write check is the strongest gate

label: The packet gates model quality before any board write: flow_check.py refuses undrawable Mermaid kinds and enforces shared rules, and its docstring names the reason - the generator silently drops Mermaid semantics.
Seven types carry an explicit nearest-drawable mapping, and the generator unsupported-kind list appears in both prose and code, so undrawable requests are answered rather than attempted.

Shared model rules are complete for a board generator: 40-character one-line labels, camelCase ids with keyword ban, per-type budget of 9 nodes and 12 connectors, palette-only colour, and no moving generated nodes.

The quality rubric adds a delete-first remove test, signal and provenance checks, but remains a prose checklist; the only scored artifact is the manual playbook seven-dimension scorecard with a 12-of-14 pass line.
Colour is grounded in measured contrast with recorded departures: one accepted pair list, 4.5:1 text gate, 3.0:1 mark gate, and seven strokes explicitly kept below the mark gate with reasons.
flow_check.py --self-test re-measures palette rows, proves each rule fails on a planted model, and runs templates, examples and claude project knowledge mirrors through the same check.
The hosted write route reuses fileKey across diagrams and revisions, treats a failed call as unproven rather than absent, reads before retrying, and rolls back only nodes it created.
Read-back compares board against model with per-type counts and degrades honestly: explicit not-possible line without a read tool and a read-visually suffix for screenshots.
Extension quality has no automated check: flow_check.py reads only Mermaid, so pins, stickies, tints and legend overlap are verified only by the human scorecard Hygiene and Legibility rows.
Delivery forbids file-shaped substitutes: with no route the packet offers the checked model in the reply and never renders Mermaid, HTML, SVG or PNG, and leaves nothing in export/.
